question.text: The IPEV Guidelines describe DCF as having the 'strongest theoretical underpinning' but caution that DCF models are highly sensitive to:

answer.text: The investee's brand name and management tenure
Currency pair volatility between USD and INR
Assumptions regarding discount rates and cash flows

explanation.text: The Logic: Per PDF Section 11.8.3 point 5: 'DCF models are VERY SENSITIVE to the ASSUMPTIONS made regarding DISCOUNT RATES AND CASH FLOWS. Therefore, they need to be used when sufficient data is available to make realistic assumptions.' The two biggest DCF levers are WACC and the forecast FCF path. The Trap: Brand and management are qualitative inputs not DCF mechanical levers; Nifty is a listed-market factor; FX is relevant only for foreign-currency investees. IPEV and Damodaran both emphasise WACC + FCF as the core DCF sensitivity drivers. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same. CFA L2 Equity Valuation quantifies DCF sensitivity using tornado diagrams. XXI-B PM exam similar. Manager's Pro-Tip: In your IC memo, always produce a DCF sensitivity table: +/- 100 bps WACC x +/- 2% terminal g (a 3x3 or 5x5 matrix). If your investment thesis requires the top-right corner of this matrix to clear hurdle, re-underwrite — you're betting on optimistic assumptions.
